messages:
ops-alert-bot: ALERT: gpu-serving queue > 95% for pool 'dedicated-nyc-g4' for 7m (throttling observed). autoscaler triggered scale_up attempts: 6, recent failures: 4. See: https://grafana.redwood/gpu/queue
oncall-miguel: got it, paging in. I'm oncall for the next 2h. Starting triage. :rotating_light:
sre-elaine: can you post a quick CPU/GPU utilization snapshot and autoscaler logs?
infra-kevin: grabbing autoscaler logs now, looks like scale API returning 429 / Pod scheduling failing due to node taints and driver crashes.
oncall-miguel: timeline: queue started spiking ~1887650340, autoscaler started 1887651000, repeated scale attempts 1887651800-1887653900. Customer 1077 (chat-agent) is seeing increased 503s per support alerts.
ops-alert-bot: Recent driver errors detected: repeated CUDA/Xid 31 in kernel: 
```
Nov 28 10:12:43 host-gpu-045 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:06:00): 31, pid=3321, channel 00000040
Nov 28 10:12:43 host-gpu-045 nvidia-smi: Process 3321 (inference_runtime) was terminated due to GPU kernel error
```
runtime-raj: those Xid 31s correlate with the nvidia-driver 525.60.11 we rolled last week. We saw a small bump in crash rates in canary but not this volume.
sre-elaine: are nodes flapping? can we get kube events for the pool?
infra-kevin: yes, nodes are going NotReady after driver restart attempts. kube events snippet:
```
Warning  NodeNotReady  2m (x12 over 10m)  kernel: node host-gpu-045 NotReady: kernel panic on nvidia module reload
Warning  EvictionThreshold  1m  kubelet: pods evicted due to node pressure (GPU driver failures)
```
oncall-miguel: immediate customer impact: throttling + 503s for a subset of requests hitting dedicated-nyc-g4. We're at ~85% effective capacity due to driver instability -> autoscaler keeps creating nodes but driver fails at boot so scheduling stalls.
platform-amy: is there a quota/scale limit hitting cloud provider? or a control-plane limit?
infra-kevin: cloud quota is fine. The autoscaler creates instances but they fail readiness probe because the driver service crashes during module init. So nodes are added but not usable -> queue grows.
sre-elaine: mitigation plan proposal (short term):
 - pause autoscaler to stop spinning up failing nodes (cmd: `redwood autoscaler pause --pool dedicated-nyc-g4`)
 - reserve emergency capacity from spare pool: move 10 GPUs from 'spot-burst' to 'dedicated-nyc-g4' (internal ticket: INF-3741)
 - roll driver to previous stable 520.x on a small batch of new nodes and test
 - cordon and drain any nodes repeatedly crashing to avoid flapping affecting pods

Can we do that now?
oncall-miguel: +1 on pausing autoscaler for the pool to stop waste. Raj/kevin can you orchestrate driver rollback? I can run the reserve capacity call.
runtime-raj: preparing driver rollback image and node-init script. Will test on node host-gpu-089 first.
infra-kevin: pausing autoscaler now (`redwood autoscaler pause --pool dedicated-nyc-g4`) -> done. Confirmed no new scale requests generated.
support-jules: looping in support — we should send an advisory to impacted customers: "We are experiencing degraded capacity in NYC region; requests may see increased latency and occasional 503s. Working on mitigation." Want me to send now?
oncall-miguel: yes, please send a short advisory. Mark affected tenants with ticket tag.
support-jules: sent advisory to customers with traffic > 1 tps in past 24h. Template used: "We are aware of increased errors and are mitigating. No action required from your side; we will follow up."
runtime-raj: performed rollback test on host-gpu-089: replaced driver package -> booted and nvidia-smi healthy. Test inference run passed. Rolling out to 3 more nodes.
infra-kevin: moving 10 GPUs from spot-burst to dedicated pool: `redwood pool transfer --from spot-burst --to dedicated-nyc-g4 --gpus 10` -> submitted, cloud spin-up in progress.
sre-elaine: monitor: queue length down 12% after 2 nodes back online, but still above threshold. Any persistent Xid logs?
ops-alert-bot: new log entry: host-gpu-102 OOM killer invoked in driver module init. 
```
Dec 02 11:01:03 host-gpu-102 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 2217 (dkms) total-vm:...
Dec 02 11:01:03 host-gpu-102 nvidia-installer: installation failed due to insufficient memory during module build
```
infra-kevin: OOM during driver build on node init — looks like init scripts attempt to build kernel modules; on some instance types the available RAM is under pressure. We should switch to prebuilt driver package or increase instance memory for init.
runtime-raj: switching init to use prebuilt driver tarball from S3 and skip dkms build. Patching bootstrap now.
oncall-miguel: timeline note to incident log: paused autoscaler 1887654060, started driver rollback 1887654200, reserved capacity request 1887654300.
sre-elaine: after rollback + prebuilt driver deploy, healthy nodes increased, queue dropping. But we still have a backlog. Suggest temporary rate-limiting for heavy tenants to protect system while backlog drains. Thoughts?
platform-amy: we can apply per-tenant throttles via route policies. Recommend throttling chat-agent (customer 1077) by 30% for 20 minutes.
support-jules: notified customer 1077 of temporary rate limit and ETA 30m. They're okay for now, asked for updates.
infra-kevin: prebuilt-driver deploy done to all new nodes, OOM errors gone on new boots. Old flapping nodes are cordoned and being reprovisioned.
ops-alert-bot: autoscaler still paused. queue now 58% (was 95%). throttling in place for top 5 tenants.
oncall-miguel: ok let's keep autoscaler paused until we confirm stable driver across at least 5 nodes and queue < 30%. After that we'll unpause and monitor closely.
runtime-raj: left a hotfix patch in repo: `driver-bootstrap: use-prebuilt-tarball` (PR #4921). Will follow up with permanent fix to avoid in-init DKMS builds.
sre-elaine: action items captured:
 - INF-3741: emergency pool transfer (infra-kevin)
 - RNT-1823: rollback & hotfix PR (runtime-raj)
 - CS-8812: customer advisory and throttles (support-jules)
 - PMT-558: postmortem + root cause analysis (sre-elaine)

Can we get a short post-incident summary after stabilization?
oncall-miguel: handing off to next oncall (sre-elaine) at 1887655200. I'll remain available for follow-up. Good work everyone. :thumbsup:
sre-elaine: taking handoff. Will keep this channel updated and start the postmortem doc.
ops-alert-bot: RESOLVE: immediate CPU/GPU flapping mitigations applied; system capacity trending to healthy. Incident classified as Sev2; create postmortem within 72h."
